milestone: Resident GPU reduction results feeding later tensor work
implementation: Bounded symbolic dependencies record per-map resident scalar broadcasts; checked helper bodies preserve original scalar/tensor operand order
Source-ordered reductions interleave with tensor maps and matrix products under one managed scalar task
One-element GPU reduction buffers are loaded at index zero by later maps; ordinary tensor operands retain full-shape requirements and lane indexing
Large broadcast maps use Tier 2 bindings; final scalar joins project away reductions used only by preceding tensor stages
No intermediate scalar readback, CPU arithmetic fallback, stage fusion or reassociation; only the final four-byte scalar is read back
Owned broadcast descriptors, signature/residency/shape validation and argument budgets precede dispatch; cancellation and failures retain acknowledged cleanup

qualification.allocation_failures: Every checkpoint observed during a successful feedback execution is injected in turn; all fail without leaked storage or argument packs
qualification.reference: Independent LLVM APFloat operations and balanced-adjacent row-major sums; exact float32 bits except NaNs compared by classification
cases: Rank-one variance over 0,1,2,3,7,64,65,257 elements with six bit patterns and ordinary/zero scalar denominators
Finite values, subnormals, signed zeros, infinities, quiet/signaling NaNs, cancellation-sensitive values and arbitrary float32 encodings
Cancellation, deadlines and device failure at each of five commands; pending core destruction; invalid forward/duplicate/missing broadcast bindings rejected before dispatch
Rank-two variance; reversed scalar/tensor subtraction; several reductions in one scalar expression; matrix products on either side of feedback; repeated interleaving
A map broadcasting 32 contributing resident reductions through Tier 2; a projected one-input final join retains the full logical signature
Eight CLI scenarios including relocated output, run with 1/2/4 workers in each mode
Installed Release compiler package builds the example; relocated applications continue to work after compiler resources are removed

remaining: Tensor-returning feedback and single-reduction tensor results
Broader GPU numeric types/ranks and device control flow
Optimization: reduction scalar last-use reclamation, buffer reuse, scheduling and fusion
